title: 2.6 NATURAL GAS LIQUIDS
summary: Ethane, propane, and the butanes form the natural gas liquids family within the broader hydrocarbon gas liquids category, which distinguishes the paraffin (alkane) NGLs from petrochemical alkenes and separates NGLs by name from methane and natural gasoline despite superficial naming similarities. Each NGL has a distinct market role and depth: propane serves heating and vehicular fuel demand, butanes are mostly blended into LPG or gasoline, and ethane trades narrowly since it feeds almost exclusively into ethylene production. These liquids are recovered from crude oil or raw natural gas at processing plants and refineries, then move to market largely through the Mont Belvieu and Conway hubs, subject to pipeline tariff quality standards that govern condensation risk.
